say: First, work out what kind of conversation you are in. Someone learning needs plain answers, not jargon.

panel.heading: Three kinds of conversation

cards.d: Ask what they heard and what confuses them. Avoid burying them in jargon.
Could they lose it all? Emergency fund? Does the person who told them earn from it?
What exact problem? Who enters the data? What does the current system cost?

say: Someone thinking of investing needs questions about her situation. Is this money she could lose completely? Is it for school fees or rent?
Say clearly: I can show you how to check it, but I can't tell you whether to buy.

say: Stay on the educator side. Explain how things work, teach research and safety, and show scam patterns.

panel.heading: Educator, not investment adviser

say: Recommending coins, managing other people's money or promising returns is investment advice. SEC Nigeria regulates this, and it may need registration.
Never collect money to invest for others. Even with good intentions, you can become responsible for their losses.

panel.heading: Educator, not investment adviser

say: Keep these rules every time. If you own an asset you mention, say so. Never accept money or free tokens to promote a project. Never run buy now alert groups.
Put the line, this is education, not investment advice, on every handout. And check the SEC Nigeria and CBN websites for current rules.

panel.heading: Your rules when you teach
items: No payment or free tokens to promote
Check SEC Nigeria and CBN for rules

say: For example, Ngozi is invited to run a two-hour workshop for 20 market women in Onitsha. She costs it before she prices it.
The venue is 15,000 naira, handouts 6,000, refreshments 20,000 and her transport 5,000. Her direct costs are 46,000 naira.
Her time is 6 hours at 5,000 naira an hour, so 30,000 naira.
The total is 76,000 naira, about 3,800 naira per person. She rounds up to 4,000 naira, or 80,000 naira from one sponsor.
Her scope sheet says the workshop is education only.

To remember. Know which conversation you are in. Use the five-question test. Teach, and leave advice to licensed people. Disclose what you hold. And build your portfolio: a plain explainer, a balanced deep-dive, and a scam red-flag guide.
